items.elements: A low, slightly drooping note (0.25-0.5 s, about 3 kHz), then five short identical hooked notes near 3.7 kHz, then a fast steep sweep falling from about 8 to 5 kHz that runs straight into a buzzy rattle of about ten pulses (1.42-1.75 s). Faint repeated notes from another bird sit near 5 kHz in the background.
items.phrase: Oh, pick pick pick pick pick, whee-rattle
items.grounds: The long low first note became 'Oh', the five even clipped notes became five 'pick's, and the high falling sweep followed by the pulsed buzz became 'whee-rattle'; all of it came from the picture, nothing from what I already knew.

items.elements: Three loud, steady, pure whistles, each about half a second to a second long, stepping down in pitch (about 4.5, 4.0 and 3.2 kHz, from 2.3 to 4.8 s), with scattered short downstrokes around them. A long faint level tone near 4.3 kHz over the first two seconds may be the same bird or a background one, so I did not count it.
items.grounds: Three long, level, one-syllable words that can be said on falling pitches match the three held whistles stepping down; I noticed the stepping-down shape is like the tune of 'Three Blind Mice', but I deliberately did not use those words.

items.elements: Six short notes slurring down from about 6.5 to 4.5 kHz, then one higher falling note, then two V-shaped notes that dip to 3 kHz and climb back to 6.5 kHz, then one loud long sweep falling from about 9 to 2.5 kHz to end.
items.phrase: Dew dew dew dew dew dew, tea, sweet, sweet, cheer
items.grounds: Six quick falling notes became six 'dew's, the single higher note became 'tea', the two dip-and-rise notes became two rising 'sweet's, and the big final fall became a stressed, drawn-out 'cheer'; all of it came from the shapes in the picture.

items.elements: Two long pure whistles: the first about 0.4 s long at about 3.9 kHz, easing down slightly; then, after a short gap, a lower one about 0.45 s long at about 3.1 kHz.
items.grounds: Two long held one-syllable words, the first said higher and the second lower, fit the two whistles; I recognised the shape as the familiar two-note 'fee-bee' type of song and avoided those words on purpose, so the words are mine but that recognition was there.

items.elements: A run of short, sharply bent notes: two high notes that rise and fall (up to about 8 kHz), two falling notes from 7 to 4 kHz, two small fainter notes, four lower hooked notes at 4-5 kHz, then four loud falling notes from 7 to 4 kHz with a hook at the end, and a final rising note.
items.phrase: Whee whee, see see, tick tick, chip chip chip chip, cheer cheer cheer cheer, rise
items.grounds: Each group of like notes got a repeated one-syllable word matching its pitch and shape: high rise-and-fall 'whee', falling 'see', faint 'tick', low hooked 'chip', loud falling 'cheer', and 'rise' for the last upward note; all of it came from the picture.
